whyItPrints: Finance and sales people who live in a spreadsheet pay so the CRM shows up there.
whyThisMatters: Someone in finance wants the CRM in the spreadsheet they already use. Superjoin pulls HubSpot, Salesforce, and other sources into Google Sheets and Excel on a schedule, and it can write HubSpot both ways. The listing says it is a HubSpot certified app with SOC 2 Type II. It showed up on the payment listing this week. Stripe-verified means the listing is connected to Stripe. I do not log in and re-check the number. The 20 November 2026 sync shows 8,780 dollars in the last 30 days, 155,910 dollars in the last 12 months, and 282,666 dollars all-time. The listing also shows a monthly line of 96,787 dollars from 3,669 subscriptions. That monthly line is much larger than the cash Stripe recorded. Twelve months of the last-30-day cash is not the last-12-month total either. The founder's pricing note says about 1,150 dollars a year per account. I am using the cash, not the monthly line, as the figure. The cash comes through Stripe. Two-way HubSpot means a cell in the sheet can write back. Salesforce is pull, on the listing. SOC 2 Type II is the security claim the listing makes. I am not treating the 3,669 subscriptions as the cash.
